extracted.intended_audience: science fiction & fantasy short story writers seeking magazines that accept unsolicited (unagented) submissions
extracted.subtask_description: A curated market guide for authors of science fiction and fantasy short stories who want to find magazines/anthologies that accept unsolicited submissions and understand each venue's pay, length, exclusivity, response time, and special restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepts unsolicited submissions (no agent required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Venues on this list accept unsolicited submissions — you can submit your work to them without an agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The whole list is explicitly of magazines/anthologies that accept unsolicited submissions; use this as a filter so you only target markets that will read unagented work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title / link to the magazine's submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the magazine title (linked to the magazine's submission guidelines page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always follow the specific submission guidelines on the venue's submission page (the list links to those pages). The author recommends checking the guidelines before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SFWA qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether publication in the venue qualifies the author for membership in the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America (marked with “(SFWA)”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the title is followed by (SFWA), that means publication in the venue qualifies the author for SFWA membership; the author notes they will discuss why this is worth prioritizing in a future post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate and acceptable word counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay (usually shown in cents per word or flat fees) and the acceptable/allowed word-count ranges for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the list: 'Analog — 8-10 cents per word for short fiction up to 20,000 words; 6 cents per word for serials up to 40,000–80,000 words'; 'Clarkesworld — 10 cents/word for 1,000–5,000 words; 8 cents/word up to 16,000 words'; 'Fireside Fiction — 12.5 cents per word for 1,000–4,000 words.' Use pay+wordcount to match your story length and expected payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the venue accepts poetry, pays for poetry, or accepts no poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many entries explicitly state poetry policy, e.g., 'Analogy — $1 a line for poetry (unlimited)'; 'Apex — No unsolicited poetry'; 'Strange Horizons — $40 per poem (unlimited)'; 'Several venues list 'No poetry.' Check this before submitting poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable authors / publication track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of notable authors previously published by the magazine, used as an indicator of prestige, style, and editorial taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post lists authors (e.g., 'Asimov's — Isaac Asimov, George R. R. Martin, Octavia E. Butler…') to help writers assess fit and prestige. Use these lists to gauge the magazine's tastes and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusivity / simultaneous-submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether submissions must be exclusive, whether simultaneous submissions are allowed, and any special multiple-submission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list notes policies such as 'Non-exclusive (response time 2–4 months, tracking number provided)', 'Exclusive (response time 30 days)', and nuanced cases like 'Non-exclusive, but no Multiple Submissions.' Follow each magazine's exclusivity rules; some provide tracking numbers or special handling for simultaneous submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average response time / tracking information
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical editorial response time ranges and whether the venue provides tracking or status information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Analog — response time 2–4 months, tracking number provided'; 'Clarkesworld — response time 2 days, tracking number provided'; 'Uncanny — response in 30 days.' Use response time to prioritize submissions and manage simultaneous submission windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notes / exceptions (genre focus, content restrictions, format peculiarities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Venue-specific limitations and specializations such as genre focus (sci‑fi only, fantasy only), content rules (family-friendly, no gore/language/sex), preferred subgenres, or editorial processes (narration auditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Beneath Ceaseless Skies — Fantasy (secondary world) ONLY/ no science fiction'; 'Escape Pod — sci-fi ONLY/ no fantasy/magical realism'; 'Deep Magic — family-friendly fiction/ no gore/language/sex'; 'PodCastle — Fantasy ONLY/ no sci-fi'; 'PodCastle — narration auditions 3–6 months.' Check these constraints to ensure story fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint policy and rates/caps for reprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the venue accepts reprints and the pay rate or flat fee for reprints (including caps for long stories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Deep Magic — 2 cents per word for reprints; $599 cap for stories longer than 10,000 words'; 'Escape Pod — $100 for reprints of any length'; 'Flash Fiction Online — 2 cents per word for reprints.' Verify reprint rules if your story has been previously published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred length or editorial preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about preferred story lengths or preferences (e.g., '5,000 preferred', or preferred novella lengths).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several listings include 'preferred' lengths (e.g., 'Interlude — 5,000 preferred' or 'Lightspeed — 1,500 to 10,000 words (5,000 preferred)'). Use stated preferences to increase chances of acceptance.
